claim: Serial focussed ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB/SEM) enables imaging and assessment of subcellular structures on the mesoscale (10 nm to 10 µm).
source: Serial focussed ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB/SEM) enables imaging and assessment of subcellular structures on the mesoscale (10 nm to 10 µm).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the capability of serial FIB/SEM.

claim: When applied to vitrified samples, serial FIB/SEM is a means to target specific structures in cells and tissues while maintaining constituents' hydration shells for in situ structural biology downstream.
source: When applied to vitrified samples, serial FIB/SEM is also a means to target specific structures in cells and tissues while maintaining constituents' hydration shells for in situ structural biology downstream.
evidence: This statement describes the application and advantage of serial FIB/SEM on vitrified samples.

claim: The application of serial FIB/SEM imaging of non-stained cryogenic biological samples is limited due to low contrast, curtaining, and charging artefacts.
source: However, the application of serial FIB/SEM imaging of non-stained cryogenic biological samples is limited due to low contrast, curtaining, and charging artefacts.
evidence: This statement identifies specific technical challenges limiting the application of the technique.

claim: Using an automated workflow, three-dimensional volumes of bacteria, human cells, and tissue were produced with resolution typically achieving 20–50 nm.
source: Using an automated workflow we produced three-dimensional volumes of bacteria, human cells, and tissue, and calculated estimates for their resolution, typically achieving 20–50 nm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results achieved in the study.

claim: Volumetric imaging using dual-beam FIB/SEM is almost exclusively applied to fixed, resin-embedded, and stained samples.
source: Volumetric imaging using a dual-beam focussed ion beam/scanning electron microscope (FIB/SEM) enables large volumes of material to be reconstructed into three-dimensional (3D) contextual maps, for cells and tissues. However, this technique is almost exclusively applied to fixed, resin-embedded, and stained samples.
evidence: This statement describes the current state of the field regarding sample preparation for FIB/SEM.

claim: There are only a few studies demonstrating application of FIB/SEM to vitrified, frozen-hydrated material.
source: There are only a few studies demonstrating application of this technique to vitrified, frozen-hydrated material (Scher et al., 2021; Schertel et al., 2013; Zhu et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to specific studies.

claim: Cryo-ET can determine protein structures in the context of a cell at pseudo atomic resolution.
source: Cryo-ET can determine protein structures in the context of a cell at pseudo atomic resolution but requires locating regions of interest (ROIs) within the experimental specimen (known as a lamella) sufficiently thin to be transparent to transmitted electrons (<300 nm).
evidence: This statement describes the capability and requirements of cryo-ET.

claim: Cryo-ET requires lamellae sufficiently thin (<300 nm) to be transparent to transmitted electrons.
source: Cryo-ET can determine protein structures in the context of a cell at pseudo atomic resolution but requires locating regions of interest (ROIs) within the experimental specimen (known as a lamella) sufficiently thin to be transparent to transmitted electrons (<300 nm).
evidence: This statement specifies the technical requirement for cryo-ET sample thickness.

claim: Lamellae are most often fabricated with cryo focussed ion beam scanning electron microscopes (cryo-FIB/SEM).
source: Lamellae are most often fabricated with cryo focussed ion beam scanning electron microscopes (cryo-FIB/SEM) (Bäuerlein and Baumeister, 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing the standard method for lamella fabrication.

claim: The current state of the art for lamella preparation uses Ga+ ion beams.
source: The process of thinning (milling) requires a focussed ion beam; the current state of the art uses Ga+ ion beams.
evidence: This statement describes the current standard technology for FIB milling.

claim: Correlative light microscopy (cryo-CLEM) for lamella preparation commonly employs fluorescent markers prior to and during milling.
source: For lamella preparation, ensuring the ROI is contained within the lamella commonly employs correlative light microscopy (cryo-CLEM) relying on fluorescent markers (usually a tagged protein) prior to, and during milling (DeRosier, 2021; Klein et al., 2021; Mahamid et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations describing the standard approach.

claim: Fluorescence microscopy under cryogenic conditions suffers from poor axial resolution (>300 nm).
source: However, fluorescence microscopy under cryogenic conditions suffers from poor axial resolution (>300 nm), reducing its effectiveness as a targeting tool for lamella preparation.
evidence: This statement identifies a specific limitation of cryo-fluorescence microscopy with a quantitative value.

claim: Shuttling between machines during cryo-CLEM can introduce alignment/handling errors.
source: Moreover, the shuttling between machines can introduce alignment/handling errors.
evidence: This statement identifies a practical limitation of the cryo-CLEM workflow.

claim: Cryo-soft-X-ray tomography can image volumes up to 10 µm thick at 40 nm resolution or 1 µm thick at 25 nm.
source: Cryo-soft-X-ray tomography can image volumes up to 10 µm thick at 40 nm resolution or 1 µm thick at 25 nm and has been successfully combined with fluorescence microscopy (Kounatidis et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement provides specific technical specifications supported by a citation.

claim: Soft X-ray tomography requires a synchrotron.
source: However, soft X-ray tomography requires a synchrotron and the resulting X-ray-induced beam damage can adversely affect the sample, damaging higher resolution features and precluding cryo-ET experiments.
evidence: This statement identifies a practical limitation of soft X-ray tomography.

claim: X-ray-induced beam damage from soft X-ray tomography can damage higher resolution features and preclude cryo-ET experiments.
source: However, soft X-ray tomography requires a synchrotron and the resulting X-ray-induced beam damage can adversely affect the sample, damaging higher resolution features and precluding cryo-ET experiments.
evidence: This statement describes a specific limitation of soft X-ray tomography for downstream applications.

claim: Serial FIB/SEM involves removing a layer from the sample surface by FIB and imaging the newly exposed surface by SEM in a repeated cycle.
source: Serial FIB/SEM is a well-known volumetric imaging technique: a layer from the sample surface is removed by the FIB and the newly exposed surface imaged by SEM in a repeated cycle (hence serial).
evidence: This statement describes the basic operational principle of serial FIB/SEM.

claim: Plasma FIB (pFIB) ion sources can be operated at higher currents than Ga+ ion sources.
source: Current cryo-FIB/SEM approaches can be extended further through the introduction of an inductively coupled plasma FIB (pFIB) generated from gases as an alternative to Ga+ ions. Such pFIB ion sources can be operated at higher currents than Ga+ (Burnett et al., 2016), thus allowing sufficiently rapid ablation rates needed to remove the large volumes of material found in tissue samples (as opposed to single cells).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and describes a technical advantage of pFIB.

claim: Higher current pFIB operation allows sufficiently rapid ablation rates needed to remove large volumes of material found in tissue samples.
source: Such pFIB ion sources can be operated at higher currents than Ga+ (Burnett et al., 2016), thus allowing sufficiently rapid ablation rates needed to remove the large volumes of material found in tissue samples (as opposed to single cells).
evidence: This statement describes the practical advantage of higher current operation for tissue samples.

claim: pFIB may reduce ion implantation into the sample compared to Ga+ FIB.
source: A potential further advantage is a reduction in ion implantation into the sample which is known to occur when Ga+ FIB is used with solid-state chemical specimens (Eder et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and describes a potential advantage of pFIB.

claim: Imaging native contrast of biological material using serial FIB/SEM is difficult.
source: Imaging native contrast of biological material using serial FIB/SEM is difficult.
evidence: This is a direct statement identifying a challenge in the technique.

claim: The interaction of electrons with low atomic number elements results in fewer backscattered and secondary electrons.
source: The interaction with low atomic number elements results in fewer backscattered and consequently secondary electrons (Reimer and Tollkamp, 1980) and therefore images have inherently low sample contrast (Reimer and Tollkamp, 1980).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and describes the physical basis for low contrast.

claim: Biological material images have inherently low sample contrast in SEM.
source: The interaction with low atomic number elements results in fewer backscattered and consequently secondary electrons (Reimer and Tollkamp, 1980) and therefore images have inherently low sample contrast (Reimer and Tollkamp, 1980).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and describes a fundamental limitation.

claim: Sample contrast has traditionally been improved by sample fixation and staining with heavy metal.
source: Sample contrast has traditionally been improved by sample fixation and staining with heavy metal.
evidence: This statement describes the traditional approach to improving contrast in biological SEM.

claim: Fixation and heavy metal staining lead to ultrastructural changes and dehydration.
source: However, this leads to ultrastructural changes and dehydration, such that constituent proteins cannot be analysed to near-atomic resolution.
evidence: This statement describes the limitations of traditional sample preparation methods.

claim: Fixation and staining prevent constituent proteins from being analysed to near-atomic resolution.
source: However, this leads to ultrastructural changes and dehydration, such that constituent proteins cannot be analysed to near-atomic resolution.
evidence: This statement describes a specific consequence of traditional sample preparation.

claim: For insulating materials, there are two primary electron energies where the secondary electron yield equals the number of incident electrons (crossover energies).
source: For insulating materials, such as biological materials, there are two primary electron energies where the secondary electron yield is equal to the number of incident electrons – so called crossover energies.
evidence: This statement describes a physical phenomenon relevant to SEM imaging of biological materials.

claim: Imaging at crossover energies stabilises the potential of the surface and reduces charging.
source: Imaging at these energies stabilises the potential of the surface and reduces charging (Joy and Joy, 1996; Seiler, 1983).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and describes the benefit of imaging at crossover energies.

claim: Different plasma gases were evaluated for their suitability in cryo-serial pFIB/SEM of vitrified hydrated biological specimens.
source: Here, we report serial cryogenic plasma FIB/SEM (cryo-serial pFIB/SEM) analysis of vitrified hydrated biological specimens. We evaluated different plasma gases for their suitability and obtained serially generated volumes with high biological contrast.
evidence: This statement describes a key experimental approach in the study.

claim: Serially generated volumes with high biological contrast were obtained using cryo-serial pFIB/SEM.
source: We evaluated different plasma gases for their suitability and obtained serially generated volumes with high biological contrast.
evidence: This statement describes a key result of the study.

claim: An automated data collection routine was developed that maximises image contrast and feature localisation.
source: We describe an automated data collection routine that maximises image contrast and feature localisation.
evidence: This statement describes a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: A range of samples from bacteria, cells, and tissue were imaged demonstrating the ability of the technique to generate subcellular information suitable for targeting.
source: Using this approach we imaged a range of samples from bacteria, cells, and tissue demonstrating the ability of the technique applied to vitrified material to generate subcellular information that may be suitable for targeting.
evidence: This statement summarizes the experimental scope and results of the study.

claim: Nascent chromatophores were observed in photosynthetic bacteria R. rubrum.
source: For photosynthetic bacteria, we were able to observe nascent chromatophores, in mammalian cells we quantified the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network, in vitrified mouse brain we observed synapses and synaptic contents, while in mouse heart we were able to observe the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue.
evidence: This statement describes a specific biological observation made in the study.

claim: The extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network were quantified in mammalian cells.
source: For photosynthetic bacteria, we were able to observe nascent chromatophores, in mammalian cells we quantified the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network, in vitrified mouse brain we observed synapses and synaptic contents, while in mouse heart we were able to observe the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue.
evidence: This statement describes specific quantitative analyses performed in the study.

claim: Synapses and synaptic contents were observed in vitrified mouse brain.
source: For photosynthetic bacteria, we were able to observe nascent chromatophores, in mammalian cells we quantified the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network, in vitrified mouse brain we observed synapses and synaptic contents, while in mouse heart we were able to observe the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue.
evidence: This statement describes specific biological structures observed in the study.

claim: The cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles were observed in mouse heart tissue.
source: For photosynthetic bacteria, we were able to observe nascent chromatophores, in mammalian cells we quantified the extent of membrane contact sites (MCS) and mitochondrial network, in vitrified mouse brain we observed synapses and synaptic contents, while in mouse heart we were able to observe the cellular organisation of sarcomeres and other organelles within the tissue.
evidence: This statement describes specific biological structures observed in the study.

claim: The degree of curtaining during milling with plasma at different currents was assessed on vitreous cellular samples.
source: We assessed the degree to which curtaining occurred on vitreous cellular samples during milling with plasma operating at different currents (Figure 1).
evidence: This statement describes an experimental assessment with reference to Figure 1.

claim: Curtaining propensity was determined at three ion currents (high, medium, and low) for four different gases (argon, xenon, nitrogen, and oxygen) at two different voltages (30 and 20 kV).
source: We determined the curtaining propensity (expressed as % score) at three ion currents (high, medium, and low) to analyse this relationship for four different gases (argon, xenon, nitrogen, and oxygen) at two different voltages (30 and 20 kV) (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: This statement describes the experimental design with reference to figures.

claim: Variations in curtaining showed a trend towards greater curtaining propensity at high currents vs. low currents.
source: Variations in the curtaining showed a trend towards greater curtaining propensity at high currents vs. low currents.
evidence: This statement describes an observed trend in the experimental data.

claim: Nitrogen at 20 kV is a notable exception to the trend of greater curtaining at high currents.
source: The notable exception to this is nitrogen at 20 kV (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement identifies a specific exception to the general trend with reference to a figure.

claim: Nitrogen and oxygen plasmas exhibit the greatest proportion of curtaining artefacts compared to xenon and argon at high, medium, and low currents.
source: Nitrogen and oxygen plasmas exhibit the greatest proportion of curtaining artefacts compared to xenon and argon at high, medium, and low currents.
evidence: This statement summarizes a comparison of curtaining propensity across different gases.

claim: Plasmas generated from xenon and argon produce the smoothest surfaces for bulk milling and pFIB/SEM imaging.
source: Plasmas generated from xenon and argon produce the smoothest surfaces for bulk milling and pFIB/SEM imaging (Figure 1).
evidence: This statement summarizes a key finding with reference to Figure 1.

claim: Both argon and xenon have a curtaining propensity under 10% at low (around 0.2 nA) pFIB/SEM imaging currents.
source: Both argon and xenon have a curtaining propensity under 10% at low (around 0.2 nA) pFIB/SEM imaging currents while argon shows a lower propensity for curtaining at greater currents than xenon during bulk milling.
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative comparison of curtaining propensity.

claim: Argon shows a lower propensity for curtaining at greater currents than xenon during bulk milling.
source: Both argon and xenon have a curtaining propensity under 10% at low (around 0.2 nA) pFIB/SEM imaging currents while argon shows a lower propensity for curtaining at greater currents than xenon during bulk milling.
evidence: This statement provides a comparative finding between argon and xenon.

claim: No trends in the accumulation of curtains or detectable changes in curtaining propensity over time were observed during automated serial pFIB/SEM on cells and tissues.
source: During automated serial pFIB/SEM on cells and tissues we did not observe any trends in the accumulation of curtains or detectable changes in curtaining propensity over time.
evidence: This statement describes an observation about the temporal stability of the milling process.

claim: The profile of the ion beam partly defines the resolution achievable during the milling step and the completeness of milling to a depth.
source: The profile of the ion beam partly defines the resolution achievable during the milling step and the completeness of milling to a depth.
evidence: This statement describes a fundamental relationship between beam profile and milling performance.

claim: The beam profile of four available gases was characterised by measuring the full width half maximum of a 'spot burn' at three different beam currents at either 20 or 30 kV.
source: Therefore, we characterised the beam profile of the four available gases (Figure 1—figure supplement 5) by measuring the full width half maximum of a 'spot burn' (see Materials and methods) at three different beam currents (high, medium, and low) at either 20 or 30 kV.
evidence: This statement describes the experimental method for beam characterization.

claim: The smallest probe size for plasma sources is considerably larger than that reported for Ga-based sources for the corresponding current.
source: As expected, the smallest probe size is considerably larger than the one reported for Ga-based source for the corresponding current (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Vitale and Sugar, 2022).
evidence: This statement provides a comparison with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: At 30 kV, probe sizes were smallest with argon, with xenon, nitrogen, and oxygen all being similar.
source: At 30 kV, we observed that probe sizes were smallest with argon, with xenon, nitrogen, and oxygen all being similar.
evidence: This statement describes a specific experimental observation at 30 kV.

claim: At 20 kV, the spot size for the different sources used are similar with argon and xenon showing an early plateau while oxygen and nitrogen increased linearly.
source: Interestingly at 20 kV, the spot size for the different sources used are similar with argon and xenon showing an early plateau while oxygen and nitrogen increased linearly.
evidence: This statement describes a specific experimental observation at 20 kV.

claim: Human HeLa cells and intact tissue from mouse brain cortex were analysed in initial experiments using the default configuration where the SEM image is formed at 52° relative to the FIB milling plane.
source: For our first experiments we used the machine in the default configuration where the SEM image is formed at 52° relative to the FIB milling plane. We analysed human HeLa cells and intact tissue from the mouse (Mus musculus) brain cortex.
evidence: This statement describes the experimental setup and samples used.

claim: A milling step of 50 nm was used based on a compromise between workflow and electron interaction depth.
source: We used a milling step of 50 nm. This step depth was chosen based on a compromise between workflow and electron interaction depth.
evidence: This statement describes the rationale for choosing a specific milling parameter.

claim: The interaction depth for entirely biological polymers was estimated to be 30 nm.
source: The interaction depth was informed by the work from Haase and colleagues (Guehrs et al., 2017) who estimated this to be 30 nm for entirely biological polymers and whilst imagining of silver beads inside cells reported an interaction depth of roughly 90 nm (Seiter et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing an estimate of interaction depth.

claim: Imaging of silver beads inside cells reported an interaction depth of roughly 90 nm.
source: The interaction depth was informed by the work from Haase and colleagues (Guehrs et al., 2017) who estimated this to be 30 nm for entirely biological polymers and whilst imagining of silver beads inside cells reported an interaction depth of roughly 90 nm (Seiter et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing an estimate of interaction depth.

claim: The best imaging parameters are between 1.1 and 1.2 kV (low kV), with a current between 6.3 and 13 pA (low current).
source: In our hands the best imaging parameters are between 1.1 and 1.2 kV (low kV), with a current between 6.3 and 13 pA (low current).
evidence: This statement describes optimized imaging parameters determined experimentally.

claim: A short dwell time (100 ns) coupled with line integration (50–100) gave optimal contrast and low charging artefact.
source: We found a short dwell time (100 ns) coupled with line integration (50–100) gave optimal contrast and low charging artefact.
evidence: This statement describes optimized imaging parameters determined experimentally.

claim: 500 slices of 50 nm depth were recorded on plunge-frozen HeLa cells.
source: We recorded 500 slices on plunge-frozen HeLa cell and clearly visualised various membranous compartments, such as nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), mitochondria, and mitochondrial cristae (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This statement describes the experimental data acquisition with reference to figures.

claim: Various membranous compartments, such as nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), mitochondria, and mitochondrial cristae were clearly visualised in HeLa cells.
source: We recorded 500 slices on plunge-frozen HeLa cell and clearly visualised various membranous compartments, such as nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), mitochondria, and mitochondrial cristae (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This statement describes specific biological structures observed with reference to figures.

claim: Two centrosomes were observed in HeLa cells, recognisable by their respective pairs of centrioles.
source: We observed two centrosomes, recognisable by their respective pairs of centrioles characterised by their archetypal barrel/wheel shape associated to a pericentriolar matrix (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This statement describes a specific biological observation with reference to figures.

claim: The distance between the centre of the two centrosomes is approximately 1.2 µm consistent with the cell in prophase.
source: The distance between the centre of the two centrosomes is approximately 1.2 µm consistent with the cell in the prophase (Figure 2E; Kaseda et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement and interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: The spacing of the centrioles is 543 nm (centre to centre) in one centrosome and 1561 nm in the other.
source: The spacing of the centrioles is 543 nm (centre to centre) in one centrosome and 1561 nm in the other, a heterogeneity not uncommon for cells in division (Figure 2E; Vitiello et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement provides quantitative measurements supported by a citation.

claim: The heterogeneity in centriole spacing is not uncommon for cells in division.
source: The spacing of the centrioles is 543 nm (centre to centre) in one centrosome and 1561 nm in the other, a heterogeneity not uncommon for cells in division (Figure 2E; Vitiello et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing context for the observation.

claim: The spindle microtubules were not observed between the two centrosomes.
source: However, the spindle microtubules were not observed between the two centrosomes.
evidence: This statement describes a negative observation in the data.

claim: HPF slices of mouse brain cortical tissue were prepared and imaged via serial pFIB/SEM.
source: To allow vitrification of tissue samples, high-pressure freezing (HPF) methods are used as samples are often too thick to vitrify via plunge freezing methods. HPF slices of mouse brain cortical tissue were prepared and imaged via serial pFIB/SEM (Figure 3).
evidence: This statement describes the sample preparation and imaging method.

claim: The brain tissue imaged volume was 844.4 µm3 (20.7 × 13.8 × 3 µm3).
source: The brain tissue imaged volume was 844.4 µm3 (20.7 × 13.8 × 3 µm3) and therefore permits observation of a range of cell types including neurons and oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement of the imaged volume.

claim: Cellular interactions were observed, including the envelopment of axons by oligodendrocytes.
source: Cellular interactions were observed, including the envelopment of axons by oligodendrocytes (visible as black contrast in images due to the high myelin [lipid] content).
evidence: This statement describes a specific biological observation.

claim: The diameter of myelinated neurons ranged from ~0.53 to ~2.8 µm (longest cross-section, mean 1.02±0.73 µm).
source: The diameter of these myelinated neurons ranged from ~0.53 to ~2.8 µm (longest cross-section, mean 1.02±0.73 µm) demonstrating that these can be highly variable.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative measurements of biological structures.

claim: Nuclei and mitochondria (approx. 87 in the acquired volume) were clearly observed within cells, including the visualisation of their cristae.
source: Within cells we clearly observed nuclei and mitochondria (approx. 87 in the acquired volume), including the visualisation of their cristae (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement describes specific biological observations with quantification.

claim: Synaptic junctions were visible, and pre-synaptic vesicles (typically 20–30 nm diameter) within the pre-synaptic terminal were discerned.
source: Synaptic junctions were visible, and we were able to discern the presence of pre-synaptic vesicles (typically 20–30 nm diameter) within the pre-synaptic terminal.
evidence: This statement describes specific biological observations with size measurements.

claim: Within one terminal, ~184 vesicles were identified (Synapse I), whereas in a second, ~98 were identified (Synapse II).
source: Within one terminal, ~184 vesicles were identified (Synapse I, Figure 3A–C), whereas in a second, ~98 were identified (Synapse II, Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement provides quantitative counts of biological structures with reference to figures.

claim: On the post-synaptic neuron, the post-synaptic density could be visualised.
source: On the post-synaptic neuron, the post-synaptic density could be visualised (Figure 3; Valtschanoff and Weinberg, 2001).
evidence: This statement describes a specific biological observation supported by a citation.

claim: The morphologies of the synapses were very diverse, sometimes with multiple pre-synaptic terminals forming on one post-synaptic face.
source: The morphologies of the synapses were very diverse, sometimes with multiple pre-synaptic terminals forming on one post-synaptic face (Figure 3A), highlighting the diversity prevalent in synaptic junctions in tissue.
evidence: This statement describes an observation about biological diversity.

claim: Such diversity in synapse morphology is consistent with previous studies.
source: Such diversity is consistent with previous studies (Santuy et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation comparing the observation to prior work.

claim: SEM imaging 90° to the milled sample surface was explored to improve image quality.
source: We explored whether we could further improve image quality by carrying out the SEM imaging 90° to the milled sample surface.
evidence: This statement describes an experimental approach to improve imaging.

claim: A compensatory stage tilt between milling and imaging steps is required to achieve 90° imaging.
source: To achieve this, a compensatory stage tilt between milling and imaging steps is required (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This statement describes a technical requirement with reference to figures.

claim: HeLa cells infected with C. trachomatis were used to evaluate the gain in contrast introduced by 90° tilt.
source: To evaluate the gain in contrast introduced by this tilt, we imaged HeLa cells infected with C. trachomatis.
evidence: This statement describes the experimental sample used for evaluation.

claim: The contrast improvement when SEM images are taken at 90° is immediately visible.
source: The contrast improvement when SEM images are taken at 90° (Figure 4C–E) is immediately visible, features within images acquired at 52° are less pronounced compared to imaging at 90° to the surface, with features such as the nucleus, cytoplasmic vesicles, and bacterial inclusions, while discernible in both angles, are much more prominent in images acquired at 90°.
evidence: This statement describes a qualitative observation with reference to figures.

claim: The outer membrane of bacteria is low contrast when imaged at 52°, but prominently seen at 90°.
source: The outer membrane of the bacteria exemplifies a case where features are low contrast when imaged at 52°, but which at 90° can be prominently seen in the images (Figure 4E arrows).
evidence: This statement describes a specific example of contrast improvement with reference to a figure.

claim: The improvement in quality would be expected to enhance image analysis and segmentation.
source: The improvement in quality would be expected to enhance image analysis and segmentation.
evidence: This statement is an inference about the practical benefit of improved image quality.

claim: SEM imaging at 52° produced a global image resolution on average over a whole FOV of 76±19 nm.
source: SEM imaging at 52° produced a global image resolution on average over a whole FOV of 76±19 nm, while using the same assessment with SEM imaging at 90° gave a resolution of 47±7 nm over the whole FOV (Figure 4J).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement of resolution.

claim: SEM imaging at 90° gave a resolution of 47±7 nm over the whole FOV.
source: SEM imaging at 52° produced a global image resolution on average over a whole FOV of 76±19 nm, while using the same assessment with SEM imaging at 90° gave a resolution of 47±7 nm over the whole FOV (Figure 4J).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement of resolution.

claim: Manual imaging at 52° with optimisation of focus improved the reported resolution.
source: Manual imaging at 52° with optimisation of focus improved the reported resolution (Figure 4G and H and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement describes an experimental observation with reference to figures.

claim: Even with manual control, 90° imaging yields more detail and higher contrast than 52° imaging due to differences in electron collection efficiency.
source: However, visual analysis of features including the outer membrane show that even with manual control, 90° imaging yields more detail and higher contrast due to differences in electron collection efficiency which is maximal when normal to the SEM (Wells, 1975).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation explaining the physical basis for the observation.

claim: The XY shift was measured to be 52±38 nm without stage movement, and 96±71 nm with stage movement.
source: The XY shift was calculated as the shift between features and measured to be 52±38 nm without stage movement, and 96±71 nm with stage movement.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative measurements of stage drift.

claim: Stage movement results in twofold increase in drift, however the absolute magnitude of the drift is small, representing under 1% of the FOV.
source: Thus, stage movement results in twofold increase in drift, however the absolute magnitude of the drift is small, representing under 1% of the FOV (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative assessment of drift with reference to a figure.

claim: For a targeted milling step of 50 nm, the observed steps were 48.1±1.4 nm without stage movement and 48.9±4 nm with stage movement.
source: For a targeted milling step of 50 nm, the observed steps were 48.1±1.4 nm without stage movement and 48.9±4 nm with stage movement.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative measurements of milling accuracy.

claim: Z-drift is minimal and not increased by the tilting regime.
source: Z-drift is therefore minimal and not increased by the tilting regime (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C, D).
evidence: This statement summarizes an observation with reference to a figure.

claim: The targeted Z step (50 nm) is achievable under cryogenic conditions.
source: Moreover, this experiment confirms the targeted Z step (50 nm) is achievable under cryogenic conditions (Chan and Chason, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation confirming the technical capability.

claim: At both 1 and 2kV imaging energy, the depth of field was found to be ~20 µm.
source: At both 1 and 2kV imaging energy, this was found to be ~20 µm (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This statement provides a quantitative measurement with reference to a figure.

claim: Using a slice thickness of 50 nm, a focus correction will be needed after around 400 slices.
source: Using a slice thickness of 50 nm, a focus correction will be needed after around 400 slices.
evidence: This statement is a calculation based on the depth of field measurement.

claim: Plunge-frozen R. rubrum were imaged in a frozen-hydrated state, absent of stain or fixative.
source: Plunge-frozen R. rubrum were imaged in a frozen-hydrated state, absent of stain or fixative (Figure 5).
evidence: This statement describes the sample preparation and imaging conditions.

claim: Minimal subcellular artefacts were observed in R. rubrum, and biological features including lipid droplets (LDs) and inner and outer membranes were clearly distinguished.
source: Minimal subcellular artefacts were observed, and biological features including lipid droplets (LDs) and inner and outer membranes, thought to be 30–80 nm apart (Tucker et al., 2010), were clearly distinguished within the pFIB/SEM image stack (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This statement describes observations with reference to figures and a citation.

claim: Inner and outer membranes of R. rubrum are thought to be 30–80 nm apart.
source: Minimal subcellular artefacts were observed, and biological features including lipid droplets (LDs) and inner and outer membranes, thought to be 30–80 nm apart (Tucker et al., 2010), were clearly distinguished within the pFIB/SEM image stack (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation providing a measurement.

claim: Collection of the R. rubrum dataset was accomplished in 2.5 hr in an automated manner.
source: Collection of the dataset was accomplished in 2.5 hr in an automated manner.
evidence: This statement provides information about the data acquisition time and method.

claim: Both developing and mature chromatophores were observed in R. rubrum.
source: We observed both developing and mature chromatophores; the roughly spherical vesicles which contain the photosynthetic apparatus and are ~30–60 nm in diameter when mature (Tucker et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement describes biological observations supported by a citation.

claim: Mature chromatophores are ~30–60 nm in diameter.

claim: After charge removal the overall image resolution remains unchanged.

claim: Monatomic gases are speculated to be less reactive at the surface of biological material, and less prone to curtaining.

claim: pFIB milling is effective for both plunge-frozen cells and HPF mouse tissue.

claim: A higher tendency to produce curtain artefacts was observed in brain and heart tissue, attributed to the greater initial unevenness of the material.
source: We observed a higher tendency to produce curtain artefacts in brain and heart tissue, something we attribute to the greater initial unevenness of the material due to the presence of lumen, facias, and supportive layers which mill at different rates.

claim: Both composition and application method of the protective layer alter curtaining propensity.
source: Since both composition and application method of the protective layer alter curtaining propensity (Leer et al., 2009), there may be gains from further exploration of different coating approaches.

claim: The use of diatomic gasses (O, N) to generate the plasma led to double images which can be corrected for but required more manual operation.
source: The use of diatomic gasses (O, N) to generate the plasma led to double images which, as we showed, can be (to an extent) corrected for but required more manual operation (Figure 6) as there was a high failure rate of automation (>80% vs. <10% for argon).

claim: The use of oxygen plasma on resin-embedded and stained samples has been reported to be effective.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation but notes a limitation of the prior work.

claim: Argon was selected as the optimal gas to develop automated procedures for vitrified samples.
source: Since our goal was to develop automated procedures for vitrified samples, we did not pursue oxygen or nitrogen gases further. Ar and Xe have similarly low curtaining propensity at low current; thus, both are strong candidates for exploitation in this workflow. At high currents Ar performed better, as demonstrated by its reduced curtaining score and visual lack of curtains. We focussed argon to demonstrate the potential of our approach.
evidence: This statement explains the rationale for focusing on argon.

claim: The use of pFIB to fabricate lamella has been demonstrated with plunge-frozen vitrified materials as part of a high-resolution high-throughput cryo-ET workflow.
source: The use of pFIB to fabricate lamella has been demonstrated with plunge-frozen vitrified materials as part of a high-resolution high-throughput cryo-ET workflow (Berger et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing prior work.

evidence: This statement describes a finding from a prior study.

claim: The effect on ribosome resolution was present despite the 'smooth' surface of the lamella and was attributed to damage introduced by argon ions colliding with and penetrating the sample.
source: This effect was present despite the 'smooth' surface of the lamella and was attributed to damage introduced by argon ions colliding with and penetrating the sample.
evidence: This statement describes an interpretation from a prior study.

claim: While a lack of curtaining is a necessary condition for SEM imaging, it does not necessarily indicate a lack of damage.
source: Thus, while a lack of curtaining is a necessary condition for SEM imaging, it does not necessarily indicate a lack of damage.
evidence: This statement is an inference about the relationship between curtaining and damage.

claim: When comparing cryo-serial pFIB/SEM images of Vero (milled with nitrogen plasma) and HeLa (argon plasma) cells, nitrogen showed higher resolution.
